title: THE FEAR THAT KEEPS US HONEST

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Do not take advantage of each other, but fear your God. I am the LORD
your God'" - Lev 25:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God repeats the command not to exploit one another, and this time He gives
the reason plainly: fear your God. Not fear of being caught by a neighbour,
not fear of legal penalty, but reverence for God Himself.

Much of our honesty is actually fear of consequences. We are honest when
someone is watching, or when dishonesty is too risky. But God is calling
for something deeper — integrity rooted in the awareness that He sees
everything.

Dear friend, the fear of God is not cringing terror. It is a settled sense
of His reality and holiness that quietly governs behaviour even when no
human eye is present. It is what keeps a person honest in an empty room.

Proverbs says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom (Prov 9:10)
and that through it people avoid evil (Prov 16:6). Joseph, alone and
tempted with no one to see, said, how then could I do such a wicked thing
and sin against God (Gen 39:9)?

This is the true safeguard of integrity. Rules can be evaded. Watchers can
be avoided. But the person who genuinely reverences God carries a witness
within them at all times.

Ask God to give you a healthy, loving fear of Him — the kind that keeps you
faithful when nobody is looking.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is my honesty rooted in fear of God or only fear of being caught?
2. How do I behave when I am certain no one is watching?
3. What would a deeper reverence for God change in my conduct?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, give me a true reverence for You that governs my life even in
secret. Let the awareness that You see all things keep me faithful. Amen.
